adjudications.reasoning: Section 3: this Basic Law comes into force on the day the 26th Knesset begins its term; from then until a committee is formed under it, the existing Judicial Selection Committee continues under the Basic Law as it stood before, may not select judges, and decides other matters only with the consent of all serving members. The 26th Knesset's term begins after the next general election, so the text fixes effect after the next general election: Deferred, stated. Confirms coder A from the amending law itself.

adjudications.source: Knesset OData KNS_Faction (KnessetNum 25) and KNS_PersonToPosition (PersonID 30814); Jerusalem Post article-847410 (24 Mar 2025), article-861141 (15 Jul 2025), article-904171 (30 Jul 2026)
adjudications.support: Noam MK Avi Maoz left the coalition in March and has since operated independently. (Jerusalem Post, 15 July 2025)
adjudications.reasoning: Attested: Maoz's post as deputy minister in the PM's Office ran 2023-06-05 to 2025-03-26 (KNS_PersonToPosition); Noam's faction membership is open-ended and the Knesset data record no coalition or opposition status. He 'submitted his letter of resignation from the government' on 24 March 2025 (JPost 847410), which says nothing about leaving the coalition or joining the opposition. On 15 July 2025 JPost wrote that he 'left the coalition in March and has since operated independently', while its count of a 52-member opposition places Noam's seat outside the opposition; it gives no day in March. Search leads (not read) gave 25 March 2025 and a Reuters headline 'Ultra-conservative Israeli minister quits, will back Netanyahu in parliament'. None of the attested sources shows whether the departure came before the 27 March vote, and none classes Noam as an opposition faction. Yes needs Noam not to be opposition; No needs it to be opposition; neither is established, so the cell is blank. Every other vote for came from a coalition faction.
